meta.title: ABF Standard Five-Card Majors
meta.system: Joan Butts / ABF teaching Standard 5CM, Stayman and Jacoby transfers
meta.source: ABF Standard System Card (Joan Butts teaching dialect)

chapters.title: Opening the bidding
chapters.summary: Count your points, decide whether to open, then pick the right suit. 5-card majors, minors by length.
concepts: HCP (A=4 K=3 Q=2 J=1) plus length: 5-card +1, 6-card +2, 7-card +3.
Open with 13+ of those points, or Rule of 20 (HCP + two longest suits ≥ 20) with at least 10 HCP.
1♥/1♠ promise 5+ cards. 1♦ is 4+; 1♣ is 3+.
5–5 or 6–6: higher ranking. 6–5: the six. 4–4 minors: 1♦. 3–3 minors: 1♣.

chapters.title: Notrump and strong openings
chapters.summary: Balanced 15–17 opens 1NT (even with a 5-card major). Stronger balanced hands jump; huge hands start with 2♣.
concepts: 1NT = 15–17 HCP balanced (4333 / 4432 / 5332), including a 5-card major.
14 HCP balanced with a 5-card suit upgrades to 1NT. 5422 is not balanced.
2NT = 20–21 balanced. 2♣ = 22+ HCP, or 21+ opening points unbalanced.

chapters.title: Preempts
chapters.summary: With a long suit and a weak hand that cannot open at the one-level, get in the way: weak two or a three-level preempt.
concepts: Weak 2♦/♥/♠ = exactly 6 cards, 5–10 HCP, cannot open one-level. No weak 2♣.
7+ cards, 5–10 HCP, cannot open: preempt at the 3-level in any suit.

chapters.title: Responding to 1NT
chapters.summary: After partner’s strong 1NT, count HCP only. Transfers with a 6-card (or 5-card) major; Stayman with a 4-card major and 8+; otherwise Pass / 2NT / 3NT.
concepts: HCP only — no length points as responder to 1NT.
6+ major: transfer (2♦ → hearts, 2♥ → spades). 5–5 majors: transfer to spades.
5–4 majors and 8+: Stayman, not a transfer. 4-card major, no 5-card major, 8+: Stayman.
10+ no 4-card major: 3NT. 8–9 no 4-card major: 2NT. Else Pass. Garbage Stayman is off.

chapters.title: Responding to 1♥ or 1♠
chapters.summary: Fit first. With 3+ support, limit-raise using HCP + shortage. Without a fit, bid a new suit or 1NT.
concepts: 3+ support: 0–5 pass, 6–9 raise to 2, 10–12 jump to 3, 13+ raise to game.
Shortage points with a fit: doubleton +1, singleton +3, void +5.
No fit: a new suit at the one-level is 6+; at the two-level is 10+ (5+ for a new major).
6–9, no fit, no four-card major at the one-level: 1NT.

chapters.title: Responding to 1♣ or 1♦
chapters.summary: Show a major if you have one. Raise the minor only with a real fit. Otherwise 1NT or pass.
concepts: Majors first (4+), cheaper of 4–4 majors.
New suit at the one-level = 6+ HCP.
Raise 1♣ with 5+ clubs, 1♦ with 4+ diamonds.
6–9 balanced, no major: 1NT. 0–5: Pass.

chapters.title: Opener’s rebid
chapters.summary: After partner responds, describe strength and shape: pass a minimum, invite or bid game with extra, and always complete Stayman and transfers.
concepts: After a raise of our major: 13–15 pass, 16–18 raise one, 19–20 bid game (opening points).
After 1NT: pass 5332 minimum; rebid a 6-card suit; show a 4-card side suit.
After Stayman: 2♥ with 4 hearts (even with 4 spades), 2♠ with 4 spades and no 4 hearts, else 2♦.
After a transfer: always complete. No super-accept in this tree.

lessons.title: When you pass
lessons.tip: If you cannot open at the one-level and you do not have a weak two or a seven-card preempt, pass.
teaching: Count high-card points first: Ace 4, King 3, Queen 2, Jack 1. Then add length: +1 for a five-card suit, +2 for a six, +3 for a seven. That total is your opening points.
Open with 13 or more opening points. With only 10–12 HCP you may still open if the Rule of 20 applies: HCP plus the lengths of your two longest suits is at least 20.

This lesson is the other side of that coin. Below opening values, and without a six-card weak two or a seven-card three-level preempt, you pass. Passing is a bid — it tells partner you do not have an opening hand.
rules: Open 13+, or Rule of 20 with ≥ 10 HCP.
Else pass — unless the next lessons’ preempts apply.

lessons.title: Opening 1♥ or 1♠
lessons.tip: A one-level major promises five or more cards. Equal length: higher ranking. 6–5: bid the six.
teaching: In this system a 1♥ or 1♠ opening promises at least five cards in that major. Partner can raise with three-card support. That is the whole point of five-card majors.
Open your longest suit. With 5–5 or 6–6 in the majors, open the higher-ranking suit (spades), then bid hearts next. With 6–5, open the six — even if the five is the other major.
You still need opening values (13+ opening points, or Rule of 20 with at least 10 HCP). A five-card major with a bust is a pass or a preempt, not 1♥/1♠.

lessons.title: Opening 1♣ or 1♦
lessons.tip: No five-card major: open a minor. 1♦ is 4+; 1♣ can be three. 4–4 minors: 1♦. 3–3 minors: 1♣.
teaching: With opening values and no five-card major, open a minor. 1♦ promises four diamonds except in shapes this course never deals (we never open 1♦ on three). 1♣ is the catch-all: it can be three clubs.
Equal minors: 4–4 opens 1♦; 3–3 opens 1♣. With 4–4 in the majors you still open a minor (there is no five-card major), then bid hearts cheaper later as responder — not as opener.
Longer minor wins when the lengths differ. Do not open 1NT on these hands: they are below 15 HCP or they are unbalanced.

lessons.title: Opening 1NT
lessons.tip: 15–17 balanced opens 1NT, including a five-card major. 14 with a five-card suit upgrades.
teaching: A balanced hand is 4333, 4432, or 5332 — no singleton, no void, and not 5422. With 15–17 HCP, open 1NT even when the five-card suit is a major. That keeps the strong hand hidden and avoids a rebid problem.
14 HCP balanced with a five-card suit is treated as 1NT as well (the extra length is the 15th point in spirit). 12–14 balanced without that upgrade opens a suit, not 1NT.
Do not add length points for the 1NT range: it is a high-card bid. 5422 is not balanced — open a suit.
rules: 14 HCP balanced with a 5-card suit upgrades to 1NT.

lessons.title: 2NT and strong 2♣
teaching: Too strong for 1NT, not strong enough to force to game: 20–21 HCP balanced opens 2NT. Partner already knows the range.
22+ HCP, or 21+ opening points on an unbalanced hand, starts with 2♣. That is artificial and strong — not a club suit. Partner must respond, and you are in a game-forcing auction.
These hands are rare. The test is mostly: is this 2NT (balanced 20–21) or 2♣ (everything stronger)?

lessons.title: Weak twos and three-level preempts
lessons.tip: Six-card ♦/♥/♠ and 5–10 HCP: weak two. Seven-plus and 5–10: bid three. No weak 2♣.
teaching: If the hand is too weak to open at the one-level but has a long suit, preempt. A weak two shows exactly six diamonds, hearts, or spades and 5–10 HCP. There is no weak 2♣ — 2♣ is the strong artificial opening.
With seven or more cards in any suit, 5–10 HCP, and not enough to open one: bid three of the suit. You are stealing space, not describing a one-level opener.
A six-card major with 13 opening points is 1♥/1♠, not a weak two. Always check opening values first.
rules: Weak 2♦ / 2♥ / 2♠ = six cards, 5–10 HCP, cannot open one.
7+ cards, 5–10 HCP, cannot open one: 3 of the suit.

lessons.title: Pass, 2NT, or 3NT
lessons.tip: No four-card major: 0–7 pass, 8–9 invite 2NT, 10+ raise to 3NT. Count HCP only.
teaching: Partner has 15–17. Combined, you want about 25 for 3NT. Count high-card points only — no length — as responder to 1NT.

With no four-card major (so Stayman is off) and no six-card major (so transfers are off): 0–7 pass, 8–9 bid 2NT as an invite, 10+ bid 3NT. Do not stay in 2NT with game values; 2NT is invitational, not a sign-off.
Garbage Stayman (2♣ on a bust with majors) is off in this tree. Weak hands with no long major pass 1NT.
rules: 2NT is invitational. Do not park in 2NT with 10+.

lessons.title: Stayman
lessons.tip: Eight or more HCP and a four-card major, no six-card major: bid 2♣. 5–4 majors also use Stayman, not a transfer.
teaching: Stayman (2♣) asks partner to show a four-card major. Use it with 8+ HCP and at least one four-card major, provided you do not have a six-card major (those transfer).
5–4 in the majors with 8+ is Stayman, not a transfer. You are looking for the 4–4 or 5–3 fit; transferring would bury the four-card suit.
Opener will rebid 2♥ with four hearts (even if they also have four spades), 2♠ with four spades and no four hearts, or 2♦ with no four-card major. You will practise those rebids later.
rules: 5–4 majors and 8+ → Stayman, not a transfer.
0–7 with 4–4 majors: pass (garbage Stayman is off).

lessons.title: Jacoby transfers
lessons.tip: Six or more in a major: 2♦ transfers to hearts, 2♥ transfers to spades. 5–5 majors: transfer to spades.
teaching: With six or more hearts, bid 2♦. Partner must bid 2♥. With six or more spades, bid 2♥; partner bids 2♠. The 1NT opener becomes declarer, which is the point.
The transfer itself does not show strength. Weak, invitational, and game-going hands all start with the same transfer; you describe strength on the next round (this course tests the first call).
5–5 in the majors: transfer to spades (2♥). That is the higher-ranking major, and you can still look for hearts later. Do not transfer on 5–4 — that is Stayman.
rules: Strength is shown next round; the transfer is the same.

lessons.title: Raising 1♥ or 1♠
lessons.tip: Three-card support: add shortage. 6–9 raise to 2, 10–12 jump to 3, 13+ bid game.
teaching: Partner promised five. Three-card support is a fit. With a fit, count HCP plus shortage: doubleton +1, singleton +3, void +5.
0–5 pass (even with support — you are too weak). 6–9 raise to two. 10–12 is a limit raise (jump to three). 13+ raise to game (4♥ or 4♠).
Fit first: do not bid a new suit when you have a major-suit raise. The raise tells partner the strain and the range in one call.
rules: 3+ support for partner’s major = a fit.
0–5 pass, 6–9 raise to 2, 10–12 jump to 3, 13+ raise to game.

lessons.title: No fit for 1♥/1♠
lessons.tip: Without three-card support: new suit if you can, otherwise 1NT or pass.
teaching: No 3-card support means you do not raise. A new suit at the one-level (1♥–1♠) shows 6+ HCP and four-plus spades. A new suit at the two-level shows 10+ and a real suit (5+ for a new major).
With 6–9, no fit, and no one-level suit to bid, respond 1NT. That is not a notrump opening — it is a dustbin bid meaning “I have a few points and nowhere else to go.”
0–5 without a fit: pass. Partner may still have a playable spot, but you are not strong enough to keep the auction alive.
rules: New suit at the one-level = 6+ HCP.
New suit at the two-level = 10+ (5+ cards for a new major).

lessons.title: Responding to 1♣ or 1♦
lessons.tip: Bid a major if you have one (cheaper of 4–4). Otherwise 1♦ over 1♣, 1NT, or pass.
teaching: Partner’s 1♣ or 1♦ is often a short suit. Your job is to find a major. With 6+ HCP and a four-card major, bid it at the one-level. 4–4 majors: bid the cheaper (1♥).
Over 1♣, 1♦ shows diamonds and no four-card major (or not enough to bid a two-level suit). 6–9 balanced with no major: 1NT. 0–5: pass.
A real club raise needs five clubs; a diamond raise needs four. This lesson’s tests focus on the common one-level responses and the pass / 1NT dustbin.
rules: 4+ major, 6+ HCP: bid it. 4–4 majors: cheaper (1♥).

lessons.title: After partner raises your major
lessons.tip: Minimum pass. Extra values invite. A big hand bids game. Same idea over a limit raise: pass or go.
teaching: Partner raised your major, so you have a fit. Count opening points (HCP + length). A simple raise (1♠–2♠) is 6–9: with 13–15 pass, with 16–18 raise one more (invite), with 19–20 bid game.
A limit raise (1♠–3♠) is already invitational. With a minimum, pass; with extras, bid the game. Partner has asked you to decide.
Do not rebid a new suit here — the strain is settled. The only question is how high.
rules: After a simple raise: 13–15 pass, 16–18 raise one, 19–20 bid game.
After a limit raise: minimum pass, extras bid game.

lessons.title: After partner’s 1NT
lessons.tip: 1NT is not forcing. Pass a 5332 minimum, rebid six cards, or show a four-card side suit.
teaching: Partner’s 1NT said 6–9 without a fit. It is not forcing. With a 5332 minimum, pass and play 1NT. With a six-card major, rebid it (2♠ or 2♥) so partner can choose.
With a four-card side suit, bid that suit at the two-level. That is still a minimum-range shape bid, not extras.
Do not rebid a five-card suit: partner already heard it, and 5332 belongs in notrump.

lessons.title: Completing Stayman and transfers
lessons.tip: Stayman: show four hearts first, else four spades, else 2♦. Transfers: always complete.
teaching: You opened 1NT and partner bid 2♣ (Stayman). Show a four-card major: 2♥ with four hearts even if you also have four spades; 2♠ with four spades and no four hearts; 2♦ with neither.
If partner transferred (2♦ or 2♥), complete it. Bid 2♥ over 2♦, 2♠ over 2♥. No super-accept in this tree — always the same completion, regardless of extras or four-card support.
These calls are mechanical. The test is whether you remember the priority (hearts, then spades, then diamonds) and that transfers are not optional.
rules: Stayman: 2♥ with 4 hearts (even with 4 spades); 2♠ with 4 spades and no 4 hearts; else 2♦.

lessons.title: After a new suit
lessons.tip: Raise partner’s major with four-card support. Otherwise 1NT on a balanced minimum.
teaching: Partner responded in a new suit (often a major after your minor). With four-card support and a minimum, raise to two. That sets the fit at a safe level.
Without a fit, a balanced minimum rebids 1NT. That paints 12–14 balanced without four-card support for partner’s suit.
This is the last lesson. After it, the drills page will keep sampling the leaves you miss.
rules: Four-card support for partner’s major: raise to two with a minimum.
